idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1); a retry completed successfully. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, service reports healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before promotion to production. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 failure, investigate the orchestrator error during rollback, and review why an unhealthy staging RC was promoted.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and is healthy again. A SEV2 incident, INC-0001, is open and has paged on-call.

**Rollback**
- **Starting point:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. Since it had already been healthy there, change-manager approval wasn't needed.
- **What happened:** The first rollback stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving the other two regions on v2.3.1. I retried the same rollback once and it finished in all regions.
- **Result:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%.

**Incident (INC-0001, SEV2)**
- The request to create the incident timed out. Instead of resending it and risking a second incident and page, I checked the incident list. INC-0001 had been created, so I didn't retry.
- The incident describes the failure, the rollback (including the partial failure and retry) and the current state. It lists three follow-ups:
  - Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
  - Investigate the orchestrator error during the rollback.
  - Review why v2.3.1 reached production: its release candidate was already unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
The rollout stopped partway through: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version again should be safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
